Reviewer: wopr pool job review-4201, GPT-6 (Codex), mkinney/Codex; did not write or refresh this PR.

Needs changes before merge. Two blocking findings.

I read the full diff and the current upstream `AGENTS.md`. I tested locally in `.claude/worktrees/review-4201`. The trial merge is `889fbdf2307a571ab3c2d8d2ab4c26bef38784df`, with upstream main `72890060b53a6dc836e8cee1d928226e11a4d753`. Its first parent is the PR head. No GitHub runner was used.

The shared edit checks all affected tools before it writes the table. The derived records take the existing `ChangeTool` checks. The original six assembly tests pass.

Requested before merge:

1. **P1: Generic delete and undo lose the assembly stack.** `crates/app/src/schema.rs:365` adds persistent tool state. `DeleteTool` saves it, but `crates/app/src/commands/delete_entity.rs:102` does not. The tree's `DeleteSelected` action uses `DeleteEntity`. I used the existing `shop()` fixture, deleted `Fly32` through `DeleteEntity`, and executed undo. The tool returned with `assembly_of(...) == None`. Its previous stack had three nodes. Subsequent shared component edits omit this restored tool. This is data loss through undo. Save and restore `ToolAssembly` in `DeleteEntity`, and add this regression case beside the existing `DeleteTool` test.

2. **P3: NewDocument retains the previous document's component table.** `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs:750` clears the table when a project opens. The `NewDocument` action at `crates/ui/src/state.rs:3485` only clears named entities. The new singleton survives. I created a `State`, added one insert through `UpsertDocumentComponent`, queued `NewDocument`, and called `drain_actions()`. The new document still held that insert. Clear the table on this reset path and add a test that requires an empty table.

Local results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 295 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `tool_library_holders`: 15 passed, including all six new assembly tests.
- `example_catalog`: 43 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored.

Extra suites run: a temporary harness in `/tmp/review-4201-probe` used the PR's six assembly tests and the two lifecycle cases above. Result: 6 passed, 2 failed. The failed assertions were:

```text
review_generic_delete_undo_keeps_assembly:
  generic delete undo must restore the assembly
  left: None
  right: Some(ToolAssembly(...))
review_new_document_clear_drops_components:
  new document must not retain old components
```

Safety checks: I separately reran `an_edit_one_assembly_cannot_take_is_refused_whole_by_name` and `an_incompatible_stack_is_refused_by_name_and_changes_nothing`. Both passed. These checks use the PR's invalid input variants. The PR supplies no source mutation list. The lifecycle variants above are red; the original six controls are green.

Goldens moved: none in this PR. No fixture, importer, or UI file changed. The extra fixture and importer suites do not apply. Full heavy lanes were not run, under the current upstream review rules.

`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is unset on this host; `review-4201` identifies this review task. The source tree is unchanged. The worktree and branch remain in place for the next review.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Review fixes for the comment on `7ce62c040`. The new head is `8fd0a47ec`. The PR stays ready (#3727). This head waits for a new review.

1. **P1: generic delete and undo lose the assembly stack.** Commit `8fd0a47ec` closes this finding.
   - `DeleteEntity` now saves and restores `ToolAssembly`.
   - The fix covers the class. `DeleteTool` and `DeleteEntity` now use one shared list, `ToolRecords` in `crates/app/src/commands/tool_delete.rs`. The list holds the tool record, the number, the body, the cutter and the stack. A new tool record goes into this one list, and both delete paths get it.
   - I searched for other paths that delete a tool and restore it on undo. I found none. The replace mode of the tool import uses `DeleteTool`.
   - Pin: `review_generic_delete_undo_keeps_assembly`, next to `a_deleted_tool_comes_back_with_its_stack` in `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders/assembly_cmds.rs`. The test deletes `Fly32` through `DeleteEntity` and undoes the delete. Then it requires the stack, the record and the body. It also requires that a shared insert edit updates `Fly25` and `Fly32`.
2. **P3: NewDocument keeps the component table.** Commit `8fd0a47ec` closes this finding.
   - `NewDocument` in `crates/ui/src/state.rs` now clears the table, next to the units, machine and post resets. Project open clears it in `apply.rs`, as before. There is no shared reset function: open loads a new world, and new resets each singleton of the current world.
   - `camcraft_app` now re-exports `component`, `component_geometry` and `connection_code` of `camcraft_tools`. A caller outside `app` can then make a table row. This adds no crate dependency.
   - Pin: `new_document_clears_the_component_table` in `crates/ui/tests/machine.rs`, next to `new_document_retires_the_machine_with_the_rest`.

The two pins fail on `7ce62c040` and pass on `8fd0a47ec`.

Gate on `8fd0a47ec3519947a09f3ca78c650b882ff72d05`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 304 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The decision file `docs/decisions/3644-component-commands.md` records the two changes.

Ready for a re-check.

Labels: **needs-rework** (one process finding, no code blockers). The PR body ends `Fixes #3644`, which closes a partial-work issue on merge; the body must read `Refs #3644`. Review: <https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4201#pullrequestreview-6079948946>. The desired label state (needs-rework, no merge-ready/needs-maintainer, no conflicts) is already in place; `gh pr edit` is currently failing on this host (GraphQL `projectCards` deprecation), and the REST labels PATCH returns 404, so the label set was left as it stands. No snapshot PNGs, no conflicts, no draft/ready change: the PR stays ready for the author's fix and a re-review.

Process finding of review 6079948946: the PR body now ends with `Refs #3644`. I changed only the body. The head stays `8fd0a47ec`, with no new commit.

Note: the body of commit `7ce62c040` also has the line `Fixes #3644`. A merge commit brings that commit message to `main`, and GitHub can close #3644 from it. We do not rewrite history (no rebase, no force-push). If #3644 closes at the merge, I reopen it with a comment that it is partial work.

Ready for a re-check.

Label change: `needs-rework` → `merge-ready`, by qsmits (a collaborator).

- NeoTech's review on this head `8fd0a47ec` (review 6079948946) says: "Ready to merge after one process fix". It found no code blockers.
- The process finding was the closing line of the PR body. The body now ends with `Refs #3644` (comment 7202514634). The head did not change.
- The commit body of `7ce62c040` still has `Fixes #3644`. We do not rewrite history. If #3644 closes at the merge, I reopen it, because it is partial work.

This is a fixed process finding with no code change. The merge follows the agreed rule for our own PRs. #4233 contains the commits of this PR. It goes back to ready after this merge.
